selected_mathematical_checks: The ring rare-mass derivative retains both useful degree-one rare sources and all four harmful sources. With A=1-w the harmful bracket is (1-w)(B^2+C^2)+BCw<=w^2. C=4K is a safe coordinate consumption bound. Each useful actual flux is bounded below by alpha exp(-4KT)/4 times its initial rare coordinate while w<=1/2.

The scalar lower bound w prime>=-K w gives the needed upper comparison backwards from a nondoubling endpoint. The displayed rho makes the entire harmful integral at most half the positive linear contribution. The doubling case and nondoubling case give q w(s) with q=min(1,a/2). The exit and excursion proof covers equality and all rolling starts, not just aligned periods.

The three simultaneous pair-sum floors exclude vertices for all later times. For a small individual coordinate, the other two coordinates then exceed m at the window start. A real producing edge and F2 give its floor one window later; for a coordinate initially above r, consumption suffices. This pays edge/vertex transitions and proves A5 for every schedule in the ring, not merely the historical numerical schedules.

At a weakly reversible siphon, an edge from a source meeting Z cannot have a rare-free product: its return path would first introduce Z without a Z reactant. A harmful rare-mass edge therefore has source rare order at least two. Integer complexes and total mass one bound every harmful monomial by w_Z^2, including all nonrare factors.

The first-order transfer graph is a species graph, with actual source monomials x_j times nonrare factors. A simple path of length at most |Z|-1 can be realized through successive PE windows using F2, padding with old-coordinate retention. The final marked edge has positive rare-mass increment and F1 gives G_Z w(s). Other positive terms can be discarded; the full negative sum is included in D_Z.

On a whole H_Z window in the patch, nondoubling plus w prime>=-D_Z w gives the full upper bound needed for the quadratic loss. The stated rho_Z pays the factor 4D_Z H_Z exp(2D_Z H_Z). The floor survives every subsequent short excursion once nonrare coordinates are bounded below.

The descending induction controls every species subset, not only minimal siphons. If all (r+1)-subset sums have a floor and w_Z<=delta_(r+1)/2, each outside coordinate individually exceeds that half-floor. This identity supplies the patch throughout each small-w_Z excursion. Inaccessible faces have a positive compact minimum; non-siphons use a genuine rare-free producing source and rolling F2.

At each stage the lower initial sum is exp(-C tau) min_Q w_Z. Hence the entry time can depend on Q, while every recursively defined floor depends only on class, graph and PE data. Larger-set floors persist at all later times along the existing schedule. There are exactly n-1 stages; no invariance for arbitrary fresh schedules is used.

The one-direction ring requires a transfer before branching in some patches, so it tests chronology. In the n-species complete degree-three family, exactly the subsets with a single species outside are proper siphons; their direct branching edges and rank n-1 give genuine higher-rank examples. Applying the stipulated ordered-cut comparison to the endpoint q_e vector therefore gives the B3 sign and strict lower bound, including all endpoint ties and arbitrary intervening label switches.
